Healthy Pancake Recipe (High Protein)

This Healthy Pancake Recipe is the easiest pancake recipe in the world and each pancake has 10-13 grams of protein!

This Healthy Pancake recipe is almost just as easy as using a box mix, but you’re getting all your nutrients from real, whole foods you probably already have on hand. Just how easy? You can throw all of the ingredients into the blender, let it do its thing, pour the batter, and there you go…healthy, homemade pancakes that are ready in just a few minutes.

Let’s take a look at those ingredients.

Recipe Ingredients: What You Need

  • Old-fashioned rolled oats: Oats provide whole-grain carbohydrates and fiber, including beta-glucan, a soluble fiber that supports healthy cholesterol levels. When blended, they create the flour base for these pancakes, adding a mild, nutty flavor and hearty texture.
  • Greek yogurt: Greek yogurt adds protein and calcium while giving the pancakes moisture and a subtle tang. It helps create a tender texture and makes this breakfast more satisfying.
  • Eggs: Eggs provide high-quality protein along with choline, a nutrient that supports normal brain and nervous system function. They also bind the batter and give the pancakes structure as they cook.
  • Cinnamon: Cinnamon adds warm flavor and brings out the sweetness of the honey without adding more sugar. It also contains plant compounds with antioxidant activity.
  • Vanilla extract: Vanilla adds a cozy aroma and enhances the sweetness of the pancakes. Although it contributes little nutritionally in this amount, it gives the batter a delicious flavor.
  • Salt: A small pinch of salt balances the sweetness and brings out the flavors of the oats, cinnamon, and vanilla. Salt provides sodium, an essential electrolyte, but only a small amount is needed here.
  • Honey: Honey lightly sweetens the batter and complements the oats and cinnamon. It provides carbohydrates for energy and counts as added sugar, so a little goes a long way.
  • Baking powder: Baking powder helps the pancakes rise, giving the oat-based batter a lighter, fluffier texture. Its role is primarily in creating that lift rather than adding nutritional value.
  • Butter for cooking: A little butter helps prevent sticking and gives the pancakes golden edges and rich flavor. It adds fat, including saturated fat, so lightly coating the pan is all you need.

Why this is a Healthy Pancake Recipe

So what makes this a healthy pancake recipe? Let’s check out the stats (I love a good list):

  • 10-13 grams of protein per pancake (see recipe notes)
  • made with 100% whole grains
  • made with no refined flours
  • made with no refined sugars

A healthy pancake recipe doesn’t always equal delicious pancakes, but these are healthy and delicious.

These are some of the most hearty and filling pancakes ever.  Must be the protein.  These will definitely fill you up and keep you full all morning long.

How to Make this Healthy Pancake Recipe

This video will show you just how EASY this healthy pancake recipe is!

Here are the (easy) step-by-step instructions. Keep scrolling to the recipe card if you’d like a printable version of these instructions along with the full ingredient list.

  1. Put all ingredients in the blender and blend until very smooth.
  2. Heat a pan with about 1 tablespoon of butter or fat of choice.
  3. Pour a small amount of batter into the pan. Cook about 4-5 minutes on the first side and 2-3 minutes on the second side.
  4. Repeat until all the batter is gone (or cook them all on one large griddle). Enjoy!

Healthy Pancake Recipe

5 Stars 4 Stars 3 Stars 2 Stars 1 Star

4.9 from 19 reviews

  • Author: Happy Healthy Mama
  • Total Time: 13 mins
  • Yield: 5 1x
Print Recipe
Print Recipe

Description

These healthy pancakes are so easy and boast 10-13 grams of protein per pancake!

Ingredients

Units Scale
  • 1-2 cups old-fashioned rolled oats*
  • 1 cup Greek yogurt
  • 3 eggs
  • 1 teaspoon cinnamon
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/8 teaspoon salt
  • 2 tablespoons honey or liquid sweetener of choice
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • butter or fat of choice

Instructions

  1. Put all ingredients in the blender and blend until very smooth.
  2. Heat a pan with about 1 tablespoon of coconut oil.
  3. Pour a small amount of batter into the pan. Cook about 4-5 minutes on the first side and 2-3 minutes on the second side.
  4. Repeat until all the batter is gone (or cook them all on one large griddle)
  5. Enjoy!

Notes

*After receiving feedback that the pancakes were too thin for some people, I tested the amount of oats. If you like thicker pancakes, use 2 cups of oats, for thinner pancakes 1 cup of oats is perfect. Nutritional information listed is for 1 cups of oats. If you use 2 cups of oats, 1 pancake (out of 5) is 223 calories and 13 grams of protein.

*If you use 2 cups of oats, the batter may be too thick for your blender. Start with 1 cup and only add more if you find them too thin. I prefer 1 cup. 

  • Prep Time: 5 mins
  • Cook Time: 8 mins
  • Category: Breakfast

Nutrition

  • Serving Size: 1 pancake
  • Calories: 180
  • Sugar: 8.1g
  • Sodium: 201.3mg
  • Fat: 7g
  • Saturated Fat: 1.1g
  • Carbohydrates: 20.2g
  • Fiber: 2.3g
  • Protein: 10.1g
  • Cholesterol: 119.3mg
